## Summary

Set up a complete failover routing chain in the proxy where requests try Qwen3 locally first, then fall back to OpenCode Zen free tier (deepseek-v4-flash-free), then OpenCode Go (deepseek-v4-flash). Configure Pi to connect to this proxy and use the failover model.

## User Story

As a developer using the LLM proxy, I want to send a single request and have it automatically try local Qwen3 first. If no slots are available, fall back to a free remote model. If that is rate-limited, fall back to a paid remote model.

## Context

- The proxy config entry `qwen3-fallback` was partially added in `proxy/config.yaml` with three providers (local-qwen3, opencode-deepseek-free, opencode-go-deepseek)
- `proxy/proxy_remote.py` was modified to support the `model` field for upstream model name override
- A bug exists in `proxy/proxy/ui.py` where `_extract_router_model_ids` is called without being imported (NameError)
- Pi needs to be configured to connect to the proxy with the failover model as available

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `_extract_router_model_ids` NameError bug in `ui.py` is fixed
2. The proxy reloads successfully with the `qwen3-fallback` model entry
3. A request to `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: qwen3-fallback` returns a response (from whichever provider succeeds)
4. The response includes an `X-Provider` header identifying which provider served the request
5. Pi is configured to use the proxy with the failover model as one of its available models
6. All existing tests still pass
data.title: Complete failover plan configuration with Pi instance integration

# Epic: Implement proactive session compaction (two-tier)

Implementation umbrella for the approved compaction approach. Evaluation
evidence and recommendations come from LP-0MTAQNAQT002L746 (F1–F5,
`proxy/docs/context-compaction-eval/*`) and LP-0MTAQNAIH001RN1S
(`docs/dev/hard-local-routing-cap-evaluation.md`); mode-specific
recommendations are in `docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md`
(LP-0MTC8BWV50012WSW).

Key evidence driving the split: 76.5% of estimated prefill work (2026-08-26)
was wasted on sessions whose context ratio exceeded 1.0 (can never be
resident in one slot → full re-prefill every turn); 99.1% of that waste is
concentrated in the top-15 sessions; decode collapse to <1 t/s observed.

## Sequencing (operator decision 2026-08-28)

**Client-side compaction first.** ContextHub has shipped compact-and-continue
machinery (WL-0MR269PDV00970YP, WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O) and is wiring the
gate-response handling (WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6). **Server-side (Tier 1)
implementation is delayed until results from the client-side effort are
reviewed.** Tier 1 is blocked on that review (see its item).

## Two complementary tiers

- **Tier 1 — proxy-side proactive compaction** (child LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD,
  DEFERRED/blocked): the proxy compacts the session at prompt-assembly time
  when estimated tokens exceed the trigger. Zero round-trip. **Strategy C
  (summarize-first) in both modes** (operator decision 2026-08-28): retain
  system prompt + very first user prompt verbatim + recent turns, fold the
  middle into a summary, truncate only as a logged backstop. Triggers:
  fast 58,300 (0.70 × 83,285) → target ≤ 38,000; cheap 43,000
  (0.70 × 61,440) → target ≤ 30,000, remote only when non-compactable.
  Enforcement gated on the quality experiment and client-side review.
- **Tier 2 — hard local-routing cap + cheap compaction gate** (child
  LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S): fast 70,000 / cheap 61,440 absolute caps; bypass
  local instantly above cap; cheap mode returns an informative gate response
  (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local prefill). Client-side
  counterpart in ContextHub (WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6).
- **Quality experiment** (child LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ): three-arm A/B/C
  validation that compacted-local quality is not worse than
  uncompacted-remote; gates Tier 1 enforcement.

## Goal

Ship both tiers with quality validated, cutting wasted prefill and
fallback pressure without silent content loss.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each child carries its own ACs. Epic closes only when all children are
  terminal and the quality experiment outcome is approved.
- No behavior change ships before its tier's gate is satisfied
  (Tier 1 enforcement gated on the experiment + client-side review; Tier 2
  is a routing-level safety net, operator-approved 2026-08-27).

## Dependencies

- Tier 1 depends on the quality experiment (design approval) and is blocked
  on client-side compaction results (ContextHub).
- Tier 1 and Tier 2 are complementary; Tier 2's hard cap is the final
  bypass guard that keeps compaction from ever being relied on alone.
data.title: Implement proactive session compaction (two-tier: proxy-side + hard-cap gate)

# T1: Data inventory & traceability harness for 2026-08-28/29 window

Inventory and validate every data source for the fixed window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52 and record method / assumptions so all later verdicts are traceable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Proxy-usage report + CSVs at `~/proxy-usage-reports/` are located; window coverage (1293 fallbacks, 381 `local_concurrency_limit`, 290 idle-time with 0 active streams) is verified against the report.
- Llama-server eval-timing logs for the window are located (e.g. `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log*`) or the coverage gap is documented with a fallback note per the parent Risks & assumptions.
- `session_slot_pool_size=3` for the window is verified from `proxy/config.yaml` (and `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` if distinct) at window time.
- A traceability note is recorded on the parent item (comment or description appendix) listing: analysis method, every data source path + time range, assumptions/unknowns (e.g. increment→Stream-started correlatability), and definition of "0 active local streams" — satisfying parent AC5.
- If any helper parse script is added (under `proxy/benchmarks/` or `scripts/`), it ships with tests; unknowns are recorded rather than guessed.

## Tasks
- `ls` / verify `~/proxy-usage-reports/` CSVs and the report that generated the 29.5%/76.1% figures.
- Locate llama-server logs for the window; document rotation/purge gap if any.
- Read `proxy/config.yaml` / `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` to confirm `session_slot_pool_size`.
- Confirm "0 active local streams" definition from `proxy/proxy/router.py:1092` (`Stream started` vs stream-end).
- Add traceability comment/table to LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4; place any helper script under `proxy/benchmarks/` or `scripts/` with tests.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `session_slot_pool_size` single source of truth (LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE)
- `proxy/benchmarks/benchmark_harness.py` — harness for prefill/TTFT measurement if needed
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `stream_generator()` / `Stream started` at :1092 (busy-time definition)
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `local_active_queries` lifecycle

## Dependencies
- None

## Deliverables
- Source inventory + method/assumptions note on parent; helper script + tests if added.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- Q: "Is an interview needed to scope this investigation?" Answer: No; parent already has clear goal, quantitative context, candidate contributors, and testable ACs. Source: LP-0MTED3OLC001RJN4 description.
- Q: "Llama logs gone?" Answer: Document gap and fall back to proxy-usage CSVs + adjacent windows with note. Source: parent Risks & assumptions.
data.title: T1: Data inventory & traceability harness for 2026-08-28/29 window
